title: Expediting Completion of HDB Developments with Longer Waiting Time
what_it_is: Expediting Completion of HDB Developments with Longer Waiting Time

sections.label: HDB waiting time support measures
sections.summary: HDB prioritises ready sites, uses innovative procurement and expedites approvals, with close to 70% of 2023-2025 flats having waiting times of four years or less.

sentences.speaker: Ms Lee Hui Ying
sentences.text: asked the Minister for National Development what support measures does HDB take to speed up the completion of those HDB developments that have a longer waiting time, particularly developments which are expected to take more than five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: These include prioritising sites that are ready for immediate construction, adopting innovative procurement practices to shorten project duration, and working with authorities and relevant stakeholders to expedite approvals.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: Through these efforts, close to 70% of flats launched in 2023 and 2024, as well as those that are launched thus far in 2025, had waiting times of four years or less.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for National Development (Mr Chee Hong Tat)
sentences.text: HDB has also committed to launch more Shorter Waiting Time flats, with waiting times of less than three years.

sections.label: Shorter Waiting Time flats and PPHS
sections.summary: HDB increased Shorter Waiting Time flats to 4,690 this year and ramped PPHS supply from 800 in 2021 to about 4,000 by end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We bring forward development where feasible to deliver more Shorter Waiting Time flats to Singaporeans.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We have increased the supply of such flats from 2,800 last year to 4,690 this year – which exceeded our commitment of 4,500 – and we will continue to build more of such Shorter Waiting Time flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: However, there are sites with longer development timelines because they may include sites that require more complex preparatory works which then limit how early we can start and we will continue to look at how we can optimise the timelines while ensuring a steady quality supply of homes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, to help them, to support them HDB offers Parenthood Provisional Housing Scheme (PPHS) which provides a temporary housing option for eligible families while they wait for their BTO flats.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: HDB has been ramping the supply of PPHS flats from 800 in 2021 to about 4,000 by the end of this year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: As a result, the application rate has come down significantly and since June 2023, all eligible applicants who are married with a child aged 18 and below, including expectant parents, have been invited to select a PPHS flat.
